messages:
Claire (Sales): Quick sync: BankCo signed NDA, wants a 2-week POC and a proposal for an enterprise commit. Key asks: capacity plan for commit, clear rollback behavior, and an example invoice for typical usage (they estimated ~1M tokens/day). Also security checklist: VPC peering, CMK, and audit logs.

Omar (SE): Got it. Initial traffic they gave: ~600 concurrent interactive users, avg response ~300 tokens, baseline qps ~9, short bursts up to 70 qps lasting 3-10m. Target p95 <= 450ms. Hosted preferred. My immediate take: pick a quantized 13B or 30B depending on accuracy. For 13B-quant here's a conservative reserve: baseline 6 GPUs + burst pool 4 GPUs (total logical commit 10). Baseline handles steady plus some headroom; burst pool covers spikes with prewarm.

Priya (Platform): Notes: with continuous batching and prefix KV caching we can often halve the effective p95 compared to naive calls. Also recommend sticky routing for session state so cache hit rate stays high. For canary/rollouts we'll use route-level traffic split.

Mike (SRE): Two operational rules to include in the runbook: 1) warm standby nodes for burst pool (always at least 1 warm), 2) reactive downgrade policy to fall back to a smaller variant if primary capacity exhausted. Add health checks to trigger autoscale earlier than user-visible SLO violation.

Omar (SE): Draft autoscaler snippet (POC):
```yaml
autoscaler:
  baseline_gpus: 6
  burst_pool_gpus: 4
  scale_up_if_qps_gt: 35   # sustained >35 qps for 90s
  scale_down_if_qps_lt: 18 # sustained <18 qps for 6m
  min_warm_nodes: 1
  prewarm_on_spike_seconds: 45
  session_affinity: true
  fallback_model: llm-lite-7B-quant
```
This is tuned to keep p95 under 450ms for the stated profile while limiting commit size.

Claire (Sales): Pricing question from BankCo: "If we commit to 10 GPUs, what monthly cost and what does 1M tokens/day cost look like?"

Priya (Platform): Enterprise discounted reserved rate estimate: ~$42k/month for 10 A100-equivalent GPUs (note: depends on contract term). Token usage estimate for hosted 13B-quant with batching/cache: 1M tokens/day ~= 30M tokens/month. Usage charge estimate: $2.8k/month (high cache hit) to $6.5k/month (low cache hit). Add ~15% for long-context sessions. We'll include low/med/high scenarios in the proposal.

Mike (SRE): Failure modes and rollback behavior to add to the doc:
- Region-level failure: automatic failover to secondary region; if capacity not available, redirect non-critical routes to cheaper pool and preserve high-priority routes on reserved capacity.
- Burst exhaustion: once burst exhausted, queue length increases and requests that exceed an application-configured latency threshold return 429 with retry-after.
- Model regression after rollout: canary and instant rollback; we keep last-good model pinned until canary succeeds.

Omar (SE): Also propose traffic replay as part of POC: capture 48h production-ish trace (anonymized) and replay against the reserved config to validate p95 and token burn. We'll publish a simple dashboard: p95, qps, batch size, cache hit, token rate.

legal-bot: SOC2 documentation package and VPC peering checklist attached. Estimated legal turnaround 4-6 business days for standard enterprise T&Cs.

Claire (Sales): Perfect. Can we get a 1-page commit sizing + a slide with 3 pricing scenarios (low/med/high) and the autoscaler YAML by Friday? Customer kickoff Monday.

Priya (Platform): Will produce the slide deck and include cost sensitivity table and commit terms.

Omar (SE): I'll draft the runbook + traffic-replay instructions and attach the sample Grafana alerts (p95 > 450ms, queue_len > 30).

Mike (SRE): I'll add the operational playbook for failover and rollback steps and the suggested alert runbook for on-call.

Claire (Sales): Thanks everyone. I'll coordinate with BankCo and circulate the kickoff invite. :white_check_mark:
